findings.evidence: template/scripts/requirement_contributions.py ensure_integration_branch gains handoff_renames, reseals the manifest and pushes. execute_requirement.py _advance_contributions adds bundle-change normalization. Neither is in proposal.md 'What Changes' or 'Scope', design.md, or tasks.md. The proposal says only first-admission ordering, the advance guard and docs. The relaxed ownership check now compares work_identity instead of the full graph, which is a safety-relevant change to the composition branch ownership contract.
findings.summary: The candidate adds a new persisted-state migration (handoff key to bundle change normalization, handoff_renames, and a rewrite plus fast-forward push of the existing integration-branch manifest). None of the active proposal, design, specs or tasks declare it. AGENTS.md requires no silent divergence: the artifacts must be updated first.

findings.evidence: publication_queue.py: `queue.append((_ordering_key(events, admission), number, admission))` sits after the try/except/else that guards only `_admission`. _ordering_key raises QueueError('admission has no valid branch for queue ordering').
findings.summary: _ordering_key raises QueueError when an admission has no branch. In _queued it is called outside the try/except that converts _admission errors into skipped entries. One malformed or legacy admission could therefore abort the whole queue inventory instead of skipping that PR.

findings.evidence: execute_requirement.py: `_refuse_queue_owned_composition(integration, requirement)` is called right after the main-checkout check, before the Requirement type and delivery mode are known. Tests had to stub publication_queue._repo and _gh in several unrelated suites to compensate.
findings.summary: The queue-ownership guard runs at the top of every advance call, including single-child and sequential delivery that have no shared composition. Each call adds gh queries (PR list, PR, comments, derive), and any queue observation failure now blocks unrelated advances.
